drafts.neutral_framing: Should Bastrop County publish all of its spending as downloadable open data, and meet the Texas Comptroller’s own transparency standard for a machine-readable vendor check register?
drafts.final_wording: Bastrop County already posts every check — as PDFs. Should it publish that same spending as open data anyone can download and search, and meet the state’s own transparency standard?
drafts.final_wording_note: Framed around a step Bastrop can actually take: it already discloses the content; the question is whether to publish it in a machine-readable format that meets the Comptroller’s Contracts & Procurement star criteria.
shaping_notes: This is a policy question about the county’s own disclosure format, not about any person — clears the bright lines.

Grounded in fact: Bastrop publishes itemized AP check-register PDFs and holds a legacy 2014 Leadership Circle Platinum award from a program the Comptroller retired in 2016; it holds no current Transparency Star. Tarrant County is the only Texas county with all six stars, backing them with a downloadable check register and a live vendor lookup.
drafts.tier_note: Open as a Tier 0 sentiment poll: no account, one voice per browser, changeable until close. Tier 0 is displayed but never cited as verified resident opinion — verification tiers arrive with the full voting layer.
drafts.background: Bastrop County is already unusually open: it posts a monthly, itemized AP check register — every vendor, check number, amount, and item description — more than most Texas counties publish. But it posts them as PDF files, and its transparency award is the 2014 Leadership Circle Platinum honor, from a program the Comptroller replaced in 2016. Bastrop holds no current Transparency Star. The gap is one step: publish the same register as a machine-readable dataset. That single change would meet the Comptroller’s Contracts & Procurement star criteria and put Bastrop alongside Tarrant County — the only Texas county with all six stars.

founding_solutions.title: Publish the check register as open data, not PDF — and earn the Contracts & Procurement star like Tarrant County
founding_solutions.summary: Bastrop already publishes every check with vendor, amount, date, and item description — but only as monthly PDFs. Publish the same data as a downloadable, machine-readable dataset (spreadsheet/CSV) covering the last three fiscal years. That is exactly what the Texas Comptroller’s Contracts & Procurement Transparency Star requires, and what Tarrant County (the only Texas county with all six stars) already does, alongside a live vendor-payment lookup. It is a format change to data the county already produces — low cost, and it lets this platform ingest the feed directly instead of parsing PDFs.

founding_solutions.title: Go further than the star: pay procurement from line-attributed accounts, so the receipt is native
founding_solutions.summary: The frontier no Texas government has crossed: no Texas local government publishes purchase-card transactions at the item level (Oklahoma is the lone benchmark). Pay discretionary/procurement spending from authorized, line-attributed accounts whose feed publishes by default, so the itemized receipt is generated by the payment itself. Reaches ~15-30% of the budget (the operating slice), framed as audit and anti-diversion, not control.
